question: When instilling ear drops, the patient should lie with the affected ear uppermost, and after instillation should remain in that position for 2-5 minutes to allow the drops to reach the tympanic membrane by gravity.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. Affected ear uppermost + maintain position 2-5 minutes = correct ear drop technique. Sitting upright with the head tilted allows medication to run straight out; the supine-with-affected-ear-up position is essential for adequate drug delivery.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The correct ear drop instillation technique requires the patient to tilt the head (or lie on their side) so the affected ear faces upward. After instilling the drops, maintaining this position for at least 2-5 minutes allows gravitational flow of the medication through the external auditory canal to the tympanic membrane. A gentle tragal pump (pressing and releasing the tragus) further assists penetration, especially when there is debris or the canal is tortuous.
